title: The Law of Attraction: Draw the Queen into a Fork
summary: Allow promotion, then use bishop checks and a sacrifice to place the new queen on a knight-fork square.

nodes.question: Can Black allow White to promote?
nodes.explanation: Black has Kf7/Be1/Nf2/g7 against White Kh5/b7/h2. White threatens b8=Q, but the king’s exposed position permits a forcing sequence.

branches.title: Allow the queen, then force the fork
commentary: Black has Kf7/Be1/Nf2/g7 against White Kh5/b7/h2. White threatens b8=Q, but the king’s exposed position permits a forcing sequence.
g6+ is the only winning move in this exact diagram. The pawn check starts driving the king into the tactical geometry.
Kh4 is the illustrated critical king retreat.
Bb4 allows promotion while preparing Be7 with check. The bishop changes diagonals before the pawn becomes a queen.
b8=Q promotes. Material alone hides the exposed king’s problem.
Be7+ checks h4 along f6-g5.
Kg3 answers the check and puts the king on the diagonal that a bishop on d6 will attack.
Bd6+ checks g3 through e5-f4 and also attacks Qb8 through c7.
Qxd6 captures the bishop, but places the queen on d6.
Ne4+ forks Kg3 and Qd6. The bishop sacrifice has arranged both targets.
Kf4 is an independently selected representative legal king escape from the fork.
Nxd6 captures the queen. The exact knight-and-pawn versus pawn ending is winning for Black; further conversion is outside this selected branch.

branches.title: A different king exit permits the blockade
commentary: Black has Kf7/Be1/Nf2/g7 against White Kh5/b7/h2. White threatens b8=Q, but the king’s exposed position permits a forcing sequence.
g6+ checks before the pawn promotes.
Kh6 tries to escape upward rather than enter the main forcing route.
Bd2+ checks h6 along e3-f4-g5.
Kh7 moves beyond the check.
Bf4 reaches the diagonal f4-e5-d6-c7-b8 and stops promotion. The exact position remains winning for Black.
branches.explanation: Bf4 reaches the diagonal f4-e5-d6-c7-b8 and stops promotion. The exact position remains winning for Black.

branches.title: Independent immediate discovered check loses
commentary: Black has Kf7/Be1/Nf2/g7 against White Kh5/b7/h2. White threatens b8=Q, but the king’s exposed position permits a forcing sequence.
g6+ starts correctly.
Kh4 leaves the king on the bishop’s e1-f2-g3-h4 diagonal.
Ne4+ clears that diagonal, giving discovered check, but this is the wrong move order: the exact resulting position is winning for White.
Kh3 is the only winning king escape in this exact position. It keeps the promotion threat; the knight cannot stop b8=Q in time.

branches.title: Independent wrong king escape gives Black another chance
commentary: Black has Kf7/Be1/Nf2/g7 against White Kh5/b7/h2. White threatens b8=Q, but the king’s exposed position permits a forcing sequence.
g6+ starts correctly.
Kh4 leaves the king on the bishop’s e1-f2-g3-h4 diagonal.
Ne4+ clears that diagonal, giving discovered check, but this is the wrong move order: the exact resulting position is winning for White.
Kg4 gives away White’s restored win and leaves an exact Black win. After the premature discovered check, White must choose Kh3 instead; a legal king escape is not automatically a good one.

exercises.answer: The bishop can check the king onto g3 and then offer itself on d6, attacking both king and queen. After Qxd6, Ne4 checks and forks the queen.

exercises.prompt: Why does the immediate discovered check fail?
exercises.answer: Moving the knight first clears the bishop’s diagonal without arranging the queen-fork geometry. The king escapes and the promotion threat remains.

startContext: The full seven-piece physical-board position is reconstructed as Black Kf7/Be1/Nf2/g7 versus White Kh5/b7/h2. The central promotion-and-bishop-sacrifice mechanism and the alternative checking blockade are illustrated. The main fork’s final Kf4 reply is independently selected because the source ends at the fork; the immediate discovered-check comparison also uses an independent representative king reply. The exact proof applies to every encoded position, not to an exhaustive tree of all defenses.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
